title: Rotator cuff
source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs; 9.6 Anatomy of Selected Synovial Joints

main.t: Four short muscles from the scapula whose tendons ring the shoulder joint and hold the humeral head in its socket.

simpler.t: The rotator cuff is a ring of four muscles that keeps your shoulder joint together.

deeper.t: They act as “dynamic ligaments”, adjusting their pull to give the shoulder joint its main support.

facts.t: All four arise from the scapula and attach to the greater or lesser tubercle of the humerus.
Their tendons encircle the head of the humerus and fuse with the joint capsule in front, above and behind.

simpler.t: They run from your shoulder blade to the top of your arm bone, wrapping round the joint.

deeper.t: The fused tendons thicken the capsule. That thickening is what is called the rotator cuff.

items.name: Supraspinatus
items.t: Above the spine of the scapula, from the supraspinous fossa. It abducts the arm.

items.name: Infraspinatus
items.t: Below the spine of the scapula, from the infraspinous fossa. It laterally rotates the arm.

items.name: Teres minor
items.t: From the lateral border of the scapula. It laterally rotates and extends the arm.

items.name: Subscapularis
items.t: From the front of the scapula (subscapular fossa). It medially rotates the arm.

simpler.t: Three are on the back of the shoulder blade and one is on its front.

deeper.t: A memory aid for the four is SITS: supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor, subscapularis.
deeper.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). The memory aid SITS.

facts.t: The shoulder has the largest range of motion of any joint, at the cost of stability. Muscles give its main support.
Constant small adjustments in their pull keep the humeral head centred in the glenoid cavity.
Two bursae, subacromial and subscapular, stop the tendons rubbing on the scapula.

simpler.t: They are like living ligaments: they tighten as needed to keep the joint steady.

items.name: Deltoid
items.t: Lies over the cuff, capping the shoulder. It is the main abductor of the arm.

items.name: Subacromial bursa
items.t: Sits between the cuff tendons and the acromion, reducing friction.

items.name: Greater and lesser tubercles
items.t: Bony attachment sites on the humerus for muscles acting across the shoulder.

items.name: Teres major
items.t: Lies below the teres minor but is not part of the cuff. It extends and medially rotates the arm.

items.name: Glenohumeral joint
items.t: The joint the cuff supports. Its glenoid cavity is about a third the size of the humeral head.

simpler.t: The cuff lies under the deltoid and is protected from the acromion by a bursa.

facts.t: Limb muscles, including these, develop from general mesoderm. Many myoblasts fuse to make each fibre.
Repeated use of the arm in abduction, as in throwing, swimming or racquet sports, can wear and tear the cuff.

items.injury: Years of throwing fast pitches overhead.
items.damaged: The rotator cuff tendons, which become pinched and inflamed and may tear from the bone.
items.cannotDo: Raise the arm overhead without pain, or with full strength.
items.why: Repeated overhead movement squeezes the tendons beneath the acromion.

items.injury: A fall onto the hand with the arm fully abducted.
items.damaged: The shoulder joint, which dislocates downwards (inferiorly).
items.cannotDo: Move the arm at the shoulder.
items.why: The cuff and ligaments support the joint in front, above and behind, but not below.

items.q: Explain why most shoulder dislocations are inferior.
model: The humeral head is supported in front, above and behind.
This support comes from the rotator cuff and ligaments.
Below, the joint has little support.
So a force on the fully abducted arm drives the head downwards.

items.q: Compare the actions of the infraspinatus and the subscapularis.
model: Both are rotator cuff muscles from the scapula.
The infraspinatus lies behind and laterally rotates the arm.
The subscapularis lies in front and medially rotates it.
So they are antagonists for rotation, while both steady the joint.

items.q: Predict which movements hurt in a baseball pitcher with an inflamed rotator cuff.
model: Bringing the arm overhead to throw.
The tendons are pinched in this position.
A tendon may eventually tear away from the bone.

check.stem: Which muscle is not part of the rotator cuff?
check.why: The cuff is the supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis. The teres major is not part of it.

check.stem: Which rotator cuff muscle medially rotates the arm?
check.why: The subscapularis, on the front of the scapula, medially rotates the arm.

check.stem: What gives the shoulder joint its main support?
check.why: The rotator cuff muscles act as dynamic ligaments and give the main support.
